preamble: The historical shift from a palatalized alveolar trill [rʲ] to a voiced retroflex fricative [ʐ]. In Polish, soft r passed through a fricative trill [r̝] (as still heard in Czech ř) in the 16th century before merging with ż [ʐ] in the 17th–18th centuries; Kashubian rz shows the same [r̝]/[ʐ] outcome.

examples.note: Soft *rʲ before the front vowel became [ʐ], spelled rz and pronounced like ż.
Wiktionary gives Middle Polish /ˈmɔ.r̝ɛ/ for the 16th century and /ˈmɔ.ʐɛ/ for the 17th–18th centuries, showing the intermediate fricative trill.

sources: Hamann, S. (2004). Retroflex fricatives in Slavic languages. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 34(1), 53–67. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0025100304001604
Swan, O. E. (2002). A Grammar of Contemporary Polish.
